standard_prerequisites.name: Scheme theoretic image: for a morphism f_i : X_i to Y_i the image Z_i is the smallest closed subscheme of Y_i through which f_i factors
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: This is the defining property used at share of proof lines 969-972
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the universal property which is applied to the pullback of Z_2 in Y_1.

standard_prerequisites.name: Scheme theoretic inverse image of a closed subscheme along a morphism, and the fact that a morphism factors through it exactly when it factors through the original closed subscheme
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at proof lines 969-971 to produce a closed subscheme of Y_1 through which f_1 factors
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the closed subscheme of Y_1 that contains Z_1 by minimality, which is the whole argument.

standard_prerequisites.name: Xy-pic commutative diagrams
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The statement and its conclusion are typeset as xymatrix displays at statement lines 949-956 and 958-966
standard_prerequisites.use: The two displayed squares are the author's own xymatrix diagrams; the shared Stacks preamble retained for this chapter loads Xy-pic, so nothing is retypeset.

core_obligations: Let Z_i be the scheme theoretic image of f_i and consider the scheme theoretic inverse image of Z_2 in Y_1; because the diagram is commutative, f_1 factors through that inverse image (proof lines 969-971).
By minimality of the scheme theoretic image Z_1, conclude that Z_1 is contained in the pullback of Z_2, hence that the morphism Y_1 to Y_2 induces a morphism Z_1 to Z_2 (proof lines 971-972).
Conclude that the induced morphism makes the two squares of the displayed diagram commute, which is the assertion of the lemma (proof lines 972-973).
proof_roadmap: Compare Z_1 with the pullback of Z_2: the pullback is a closed subscheme of Y_1 through which f_1 factors, so minimality of Z_1 gives the induced morphism (proof lines 969-973).
difficulty_reason: The statement is that in a commutative square of schemes the scheme theoretic images Z_i of the horizontal maps are connected by an induced morphism Z_1 to Z_2, giving the displayed commutative diagram (statement lines 948-967). The proof is three lines and its content is a universal-property argument: the scheme theoretic inverse image of Z_2 in Y_1 is a closed subscheme through which f_1 factors, so the minimality of the scheme theoretic image Z_1 puts Z_1 inside that pullback, which is exactly the induced morphism (proof lines 969-973). It is H2: the argument is complete and short, and the only inputs are the definition of the scheme theoretic image and of the scheme theoretic inverse image; the two xymatrix displays are the author's own and were not redrawn.
